text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian air traffic controllers have given airport authorities a 21-day ultimatum to improve poor navigational facilities or face strike action.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation has sent a coastal tanker to southern Warri oil refinery to bring an estimated 12,000 tonnes of fuel to Lagos.
- The first shipment of liquefied petroleum gas from Chevron's Escravos Gas project is likely to be exported later this month, after government gives clearance.
- Business Times investigations show that foreign partners of pharmaceutical firm May and Baker are trying to divest from the company, by renouncing their stake in a rights issue.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha reminds soldiers of their subordinate role to civilian authorities.
- Two proposals, involving sale of assets and a swap of equity for deposits, are being put forward as ways to salvage Nigeria Merchant Bank from liquidation.

- Officials say the government is not bothered by the outcome of a meeting on Thursday between the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group and four pro-democracy groups, to discuss Nigeria's suspension from the Commonwealth.
- Ethnic Itsekiris in the southern oil-producing area near Warri have sent an appeal to Abacha, asking for protection. The Itsekiris say Ijaw tribesmen are preparing to attack them.
